source_text:
Εἶδες οἵους τοῖς αὐτῆς δεομένοις βλαστάνει καρπούς,
πῶς τὰς μὲν πηγὰς τῆς πορνείας ξηραίνει, τὰς δὲ ξηρανθείσας τῇ στειρώσει μήτρας
ἀνοίγει καὶ τὰς ἐκ τῶν λογισμῶν δὲ φυομένας ἀκάνθας τῆς ἁμαρτίας ἐκκόπτει καὶ

τοὺς τῆς ἀσεβείας οὐκέτι δίδωσιν καρπούς. Οὐ μόνον δὲ δύναται ταῦτα ἡ κατὰ θεὸν
νηστεία, ἀλλὰ καὶ ἡμέρους τοὺς ἀπηνεῖς ἀπεργάζεται καὶ εἰς συμπάθειαν τοὺς
ἀσυμπαθεῖς μεταβάλλει, τὸ σκληρὸν τῶν ἀνενδότων μαλάσσει χαλκεύουσα.
9 Αὕτη οὐ μόνον ἁμαρτωλοῖς χρήσιμος, ἀλλ' ἤδη καὶ δικαίοις εἰς καιρὸν
ἐπιτήδειος, ὡς προεδείξαμεν. Νηστεύσας Μωυσῆς τεσσαράκοντα ἡμέρας καὶ
τεσσαράκοντα νύκτας εἰς ἐκεῖνον εἰσῆλθεν τὸν γνόφον, καὶ εἶδεν θεὸν ὡς οὐδενὶ
ἀνθρώπων ἐγγέγονεν, κατὰ τὴν αὐτοῦ τοῦ θεοῦ περὶ αὐτοῦ μαρτυρίαν λέγοντος·
«Ἐὰν γένηται προφήτης ἐν ὑμῖν τῷ κυρίῳ, ἐν ὁράματι αὐτῷ γνωσθήσομαι καὶ ἐν
ὕπνῳ λαλήσω αὐτῷ. Οὐχ ὣς ὁ θεράπων μου Μωυσῆς, στόμα κατὰ στόμα», πρόσωπον
πρὸς πρόσωπον, «ὡς ἐάν τις λαλήσῃ πρὸς τὸν ἑαυτοῦ φίλον.» Ταύτην ἐξαίρετον
θέαν ἡ νηστεία τῷ προφήτῃ κεκόμικεν δῶρον καὶ τὸ πρόσωπον τοῦ νηστεύσαντος
εἰς θειοτέραν τινὰ φωτὸς ἀπροσίτου ἀστραπὴν μετέθηκεν καὶ δέδωκεν τῷ προφήτῃ
δέλτους δακτύλῳ θεοῦ γεγραμμένας
10 Προσερχώμεθα τοίνυν αὐτῇ μετὰ φαιδροῦ τοῦ προσώπου, ἱλαροὶ ταῖς
ψυχαῖς αὐτὴν ἀσπασώμεθα καὶ μὴ βρωμάτων μὲν ἀπεχώμεθα, ἁμαρτημάτων δὲ
2
ἀντεχώμεθα· μηδὲ ταπεινοὶ τῷ προσώπῳ τοῖς ἀνθρώποις δεικνύμενοι, ὑπερήφανοι
τῇ ψυχῇ τῷ δεσπότῃ φανῶμεν· καὶ πένησιν διδόντες, μὴ ἄλλους ἁρπάσωμεν· καὶ
θεὸν κολακεύοντες λόγοις, μὴ ἔργῳ τοὺς ἀδελφοὺς ἡμῶν κατασφάξωμεν,
μνημονεύοντες ἀεὶ τοῦ ἀποστόλου λέγοντος· «Εἰρήνην διώκετε μετὰ πάντων καὶ
τὸν ἁγιασμόν, οὗ χωρὶς οὐδεὶς ὄψεται τὸν κύριον.» Ἀλλ' ἐκ πάντων τῶν κακῶν μετὰ
βρωμάτων νηστεύοντες, λέγωμεν πρὸς αὐτόν· «Ἐλεεῖς δὲ πάντας, ὅτι πάντα
δύνασαι, καὶ παρορᾷς ἁμαρτήματα ἀνθρώπων εἰς μετάνοιαν»· ὅτι σοι πρέπει πᾶσα
δόξα τῷ Πατρὶ καὶ τῷ Υἱῷ καὶ τῷ ἁγίῳ Πνεύματι, νῦν καὶ ἀεὶ καὶ εἰς τοὺς αἰῶνας
τῶν αἰώνων. Ἀμήν.

3
thought_title: Fasting's fruits, Moses' vision, and a closing exhortation
orientation: Hesychius is closing his homily, having just shown how fasting gave Samuel to Hannah; he now sums up fasting's power, holds up Moses' fast and vision of God as its crowning gift, and urges the congregation to fast from all evils, not only foods.
pass_a_gloss: You have seen what kind of fruits it produces for those who ask of it, how it dries up the springs of fornication, and opens the wombs that have been dried up by barrenness, and cuts out the thorns of sin that grow from the thoughts, and no longer gives the fruits of impiety. Not only is the fasting according to God able to do these things, but it also makes the harsh gentle and changes the uncompassionate into compassion, softening the hardness of the unyielding as it works bronze. This is not only useful for sinners, but already also suitable for the righteous in season, as we showed before. Moses, having fasted forty days and forty nights, entered into that darkness, and saw God as has happened to no one of humans, according to the testimony of God himself about him, saying: 'If there becomes a prophet among you to the Lord, in a vision I will be known to him and in sleep I will speak to him. Not so as my servant Moses, mouth to mouth,' face to face, 'as if someone will speak to his own friend.' This exceptional sight fasting has brought to the prophet as a gift, and the face of the one who fasted it changed into a more divine lightning-flash of unapproachable light, and it gave to the prophet tablets written by the finger of God. Let us therefore come to it with a bright face, let us greet it cheerful in our souls, and let us not abstain from foods but hold fast to sins; nor let us appear humble in face to humans, and be shown proud in soul to the master; and while giving to the poor, let us not rob others; and while flattering God with words, let us not slaughter our brothers in deed, remembering always the apostle saying: 'Pursue peace with all and the holiness, without which no one will see the Lord.' But fasting from all evils along with foods, let us say to him: 'But you have mercy on all, because you can do all things, and you overlook the sins of humans for repentance'; because to you is fitting all glory, to the Father and to the Son and to the Holy Spirit, now and always and to the ages of ages. Amen.

choices.why: The participle is nominative feminine singular, agreeing with νηστεία (fasting) as the subject; it describes fasting itself performing the action of a bronzesmith, softening hard metal.
The article points to the specific darkness of Sinai where Moses met God; 'that darkness' preserves the demonstrative force.
The perfect of γίγνομαι with dative means 'has come to be for' or 'has happened to'; rendering it as 'has happened to no one of humans' keeps the dative force.
The noun means a flash of lightning; 'lightning-flash' preserves the vivid image of the unapproachable light.
ἀντέχομαι with genitive means 'hold fast to' or 'cling to'; the contrast with ἀπεχώμεθα (abstain from) requires a strong positive verb.
The verb means to slaughter or butcher; it is deliberately violent, matching the homily's earlier examples of fasting used for murder.

bible_refs.note: Ἐὰν γένηται προφήτης ἐν ὑμῖν τῷ κυρίῳ, ἐν ὁράματι αὐτῷ γνωσθήσομαι καὶ ἐν ὕπνῳ λαλήσω αὐτῷ. Οὐχ ὣς ὁ θεράπων μου Μωυσῆς, στόμα κατὰ στόμα, πρόσωπον πρὸς πρόσωπον, ὡς ἐάν τις λαλήσῃ πρὸς τὸν ἑαυτοῦ φίλον.
Εἰρήνην διώκετε μετὰ πάντων καὶ τὸν ἁγιασμόν, οὗ χωρὶς οὐδεὶς ὄψεται τὸν κύριον.
Ἐλεεῖς δὲ πάντας, ὅτι πάντα δύνασαι, καὶ παρορᾷς ἁμαρτήματα ἀνθρώπων εἰς μετάνοιαν.

pass_b_english: You have seen what fruits it produces for those who ask of it: how it dries up the springs of fornication, opens wombs that barrenness had dried shut, cuts out the thorns of sin that grow from our thoughts, and no longer allows the fruits of impiety to appear. Fasting according to God can do all this, and more: it makes the harsh gentle, turns the pitiless toward compassion, and softens the hard metal of the unyielding as it works bronze.

This fasting is useful not only for sinners but also, at the right time, for the righteous, as we have already shown. Moses fasted forty days and forty nights, entered that darkness, and saw God as has happened to no one among human beings, according to the testimony of God himself about him, saying: “If there is a prophet among you who belongs to the Lord, I will make myself known to him in a vision and speak to him in a dream. Not so with my servant Moses; mouth to mouth, face to face, as one speaks to his own friend” (Numbers 12:6-8). Fasting brought this extraordinary sight to the prophet as a gift, changed the face of the one who fasted into a kind of divine lightning-flash of unapproachable light, and gave the prophet tablets written by the finger of God.

Let us therefore approach fasting with a bright face. Let us greet it with joyful souls, and let us not abstain from foods while holding fast to sins. Let us not show ourselves humble in appearance before people while appearing arrogant in soul before the Master. Let us not give to the poor while robbing others. Let us not flatter God with words while slaughtering our brothers and sisters in deed, remembering always the apostle saying: “Pursue peace with everyone, and the holiness without which no one will see the Lord” (Hebrews 12:14). But fasting from all evils along with foods, let us say to him: “You have mercy on all, because you can do all things, and you overlook the sins of human beings for repentance” (Wisdom of Solomon 11:23). For to you belongs all glory, to the Father and to the Son and to the Holy Spirit, now and always and to the ages of ages. Amen.

last_rejected.quote: and no longer allows the fruits of impiety to appear
last_rejected.source_quote: τοὺς τῆς ἀσεβείας οὐκέτι δίδωσιν καρπούς
last_rejected.why: Source says 'no longer gives fruits to impiety,' i.e., stops impiety from bearing fruit. English says fruits don't 'appear' — weaker and different sense.
last_rejected.fix: and no longer allows impiety to bear fruit
last_rejected.ruling: δίδωσιν καρπούς = 'gives fruits'; 'allows to appear' is interpretive but captures cessation of fruit-bearing.

last_rejected.why: Source says fasting makes the harsh 'gentle' (ἡμέρους), not 'the harsh gentle' as if 'harsh' is a noun. Grammar: 'makes the harsh ones gentle.'
last_rejected.ruling: 'makes the harsh gentle' is standard English adjective-to-adjective construction; meaning identical.

last_rejected.quote: I will make myself known to him in a vision
last_rejected.why: Source: 'I will be known to him in a vision.' The English 'make myself known to him' changes the passive to active, shifting agency.
last_rejected.fix: I will be known to him in a vision
last_rejected.ruling: γνωσθήσομαι is divine passive; 'make myself known' is conventional English rendering of Hebrew idiom.

last_rejected.source_quote: τὸ σκληρὸν τῶν ἀνενδότων μαλάσσει χαλκεύουσα
last_rejected.why: χαλκεύουσα means 'smithing/forging,' not 'works bronze'; metaphor is misrendered.
last_rejected.fix: softens the hard metal of the unyielding as a smith forges it
last_rejected.ruling: χαλκεύουσα means 'working bronze'; 'works bronze' is literal and correct, not a mistranslation.

last_rejected.why: ἀντεχώμεθα means 'let us cling to/hold onto,' but context demands 'let us abstain from' as parallel to ἀπεχώμεθα.
last_rejected.fix: let us not abstain from foods while clinging to sins
last_rejected.ruling: ἀντεχώμεθα means 'hold fast/cling'; context is ironic contrast with ἀπεχώμεθα, correctly rendered.

last_rejected.quote: Let us not give to the poor while robbing others
last_rejected.source_quote: καὶ πένησιν διδόντες, μὴ ἄλλους ἁρπάσωμεν
last_rejected.why: πένησιν διδόντες is positive command 'giving to the poor,' not negative; structure is 'while giving... let us not rob.'
last_rejected.fix: while giving to the poor, let us not rob others
last_rejected.ruling: English correctly captures 'giving to the poor, let us not rob others'; parallel structure is accurately rendered.

last_rejected.quote: slaughtering our brothers and sisters in deed
last_rejected.source_quote: μὴ ἔργῳ τοὺς ἀδελφοὺς ἡμῶν κατασφάξωμεν
last_rejected.why: ἀδελφοὺς is masculine plural 'brothers,' not gender-inclusive; no textual basis for 'sisters.'
last_rejected.ruling: ἀδελφοὺς can include both genders inclusively; 'brothers and sisters' is standard acceptable rendering.
